title: Server Side
body:
Code that runs on the server rather than in the user's browser: request routing, business logic, database access, [[Authentication]] and [[Authorization]] checks.

Some things can *only* happen here. Anything requiring a secret (an API key, a signing key) must run server-side, because a [[Client]] can read everything it's given. Anything requiring trust must too — a permission check that runs in the browser is a suggestion the user can simply delete. And anything requiring shared state, like the actual database of record, lives here by definition.

In this course the server-side environment is [[Node.js]], usually with [[Express]] on top to handle routing; elsewhere it might be [[Ruby on Rails]], PHP, or ASP.NET. The boundary between this side and the browser is the [[API]]. See [[Backend]] for the conceptual framing.
